scope: Selective primary-source reading of relevant sections; not an exhaustive review and not a claim to have read every appendix or replication.

sources.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
sources.version_read: Published paper, university-hosted copy
sources.read_depth: Relevant full-text sections: evaluation equations around pp. 275–277; reference-point translation and framing around pp. 286–289; abstract/introduction.
sources.evidence_type: Descriptive decision theory supported by choice problems
sources.claim: Gains/losses are reference-dependent; decision weighting and value curvature are distinct.
sources.causal_strength: Supports choice-level departures under specific elicitation; no identified aggregate-price effect.
limitations: Choice evidence does not identify market-level demand
Reference point is not automatically purchase price
No universal production parameter values inferred

sources.title: Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses?
sources.version_read: Published paper, author-hosted PDF; alternate author URL redirects vary by capitalization
sources.read_depth: Full-text PGR/PLR construction, hypotheses/results, subgroup table, rebalancing discussion, and conclusion.
sources.claim: Greater gain than loss realization, with December variation and tests of alternative explanations.
sources.causal_strength: Direct behavior measurement; psychological cause not uniquely identified.
limitations: Historical brokerage population
Joint test of reference coding and disposition behavior
Not proof every loser should be sold

sources.title: Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors
sources.version_read: April 1999 author draft hosted by Penn State CiteSeerX
sources.read_depth: Abstract, turnover-quintile design, gross/net performance and competing overconfidence versus rational-information predictions around draft pp. 18–20.
sources.claim: High household turnover was associated with lower net performance in the sample; consistent with excessive trading.
sources.causal_strength: Strong direct account observations; indirect inference about overconfidence.
limitations: No randomized overconfidence treatment
Historical commission and execution regime
Working-paper version inspected

sources.title: All That Glitters: The Effect of Attention and News on the Buying Behavior of Individual and Institutional Investors
sources.version_read: Published paper; November 2002 working draft also inspected before published copy located
sources.read_depth: Data description, abnormal-volume/return/news sorts, published results and conclusion, alternative short-selling/heterogeneous-belief explanation around pp. 809–811.
sources.evidence_type: Observational account/order data plus formal explanation
sources.claim: Attention-grabbing stocks attract disproportionate net buying by sampled individuals; institutions differ by style.
sources.causal_strength: Behavioral association with robustness checks; attention proxies can be endogenous.
limitations: Attention and information may co-move
Institutions are heterogeneous
Historical platform/trading environment

sources.title: Investor Inattention and Friday Earnings Announcements
sources.version_read: October 2005 NBER working paper 11683, titled Investor Inattention, Firm Reaction, and Friday Earnings Announcements; published bibliographic record checked
sources.read_depth: Working-paper homogeneous-sample selection discussion, Section 4 stock return response, Section 6 firm reaction, Section 8 conclusion.
sources.evidence_type: Observational event comparison with selection controls
sources.claim: Friday earnings releases show weaker immediate and stronger delayed response in the studied sample.
sources.causal_strength: Suggestive attention mechanism, not randomized weekday assignment.
limitations: Firm timing selection
Working-paper versus published estimates may differ
No assertion of current tradable Friday premium

sources.title: Expectations of Returns and Expected Returns
sources.version_read: Published author-hosted paper
sources.read_depth: Introduction, survey-source definitions, extrapolation discussion, Table 5 comparison of survey expectations and model-based expected-return measures.
sources.claim: Survey expectations tend to be extrapolative and differ from valuation-based expected-return proxies.
sources.causal_strength: Directly measures reported expectations; not randomized belief formation.
limitations: Survey-population selection
Expected-return proxies are model-dependent
No one-to-one mapping from survey mean to marginal trader

sources.title: Diagnostic Expectations and Stock Returns
sources.version_read: Published paper
sources.read_depth: Diagnostic updating discussion, forecast-error/revision regression proposition, Section VI distinguishing kernel-of-truth predictions, explicit model-fit limitations near pp. 2864–2865.
sources.evidence_type: Formal behavioral model plus observational analyst/fundamental tests
sources.claim: Representativeness can exaggerate genuine shifts in the prevalence of exceptional outcomes.
sources.causal_strength: Distinctive testable restrictions with supportive evidence; not randomized psychological mechanism.
limitations: Analyst forecasts may reflect incentives
Model abstracts from heterogeneity
Authors note qualitative features not captured

sources.title: Depression Babies: Do Macroeconomic Experiences Affect Risk-Taking?
sources.version_read: March 2009 NBER working paper 14813
sources.read_depth: Data/abstract, Section III elicited-risk-aversion design, age/year/cohort identification and reverse-causality discussion.
sources.claim: Experienced lifetime returns relate to later risk taking and market participation.
sources.causal_strength: Identification uses cross-sectional differences and their time variation; experience histories are not randomized.
limitations: Age/period/cohort identification requires structure
Experiences may correlate with other unobserved influences
Working version read

sources.title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades
sources.version_read: Published university-hosted copy
sources.read_depth: Introduction distinguishing conformity mechanisms; sequential-information argument; Proposition 1 and incorrect-cascade discussion.
sources.claim: Rational action imitation can stop private information from entering public behavior.
sources.causal_strength: Logical mechanism under assumptions, not a market prevalence estimate.
limitations: Discrete sequential choices differ from continuous-price markets
Signal/information assumptions matter
Agreement is not proof of a cascade

sources.title: Information Cascades in the Laboratory
sources.version_read: University-hosted full-text manuscript of published work
sources.read_depth: Introduction, symmetric model, experimental procedures, Section III results and observed cascade opportunities.
sources.claim: Sequential prediction tasks exhibit cascade behavior under known signal structures.
sources.causal_strength: Strong control of information environment; limited market external validity.
limitations: Urn task is not an exchange
Repeated choices within sessions are dependent
Not a direct return forecast

sources.title: Herd Behavior and Investment
sources.version_read: Published university-hosted copy
sources.read_depth: Abstract/introduction, signal assumptions, timing/information structure, managerial objectives and reputation channel.
sources.claim: Reputational incentives can make imitation individually rational despite social inefficiency.
sources.causal_strength: Theoretical conditional mechanism only.
limitations: Requires empirical evidence of incentives and choices in any application
Common fundamentals can also produce similar investments

sources.title: Echo Chambers
sources.version_read: February 14, 2022 author manuscript; publication record checked
sources.read_depth: Introduction/sample description and user/user-symbol plus symbol-day fixed-effects design; following-homophily results and uncertainty boundary.
sources.claim: Investors selectively expose themselves to confirmatory views; network structure sustains disagreement.
sources.causal_strength: Rich within-firm/date design; no randomized feed assignment.
limitations: Platform selection
Expressed views need not equal funded positions
Network choice is endogenous
Trading/return associations not direct causal intervention effects

sources.title: Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
sources.version_read: Author-hosted full-text manuscript identifying definitive journal version
sources.read_depth: Pessimism-factor construction, newspaper/newswire publication timing, market-activity regressions and reverse feedback discussion.
sources.claim: Media pessimism is related to subsequent prices/volume, with feedback from past returns to media.
sources.causal_strength: Predictive timing does not by itself establish exogenous media causality.
limitations: Recurring column partly describes prior market activity
Historical media regime
Publication and executable receipt times differ

sources.title: Narrative Economics
sources.version_read: January 2017 Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper 2069 / presidential address; published record checked
sources.read_depth: Introduction and epidemic-model sections, SIR mechanics, social-diffusion qualifications and behavioral-residue distinction.
sources.evidence_type: Conceptual framework, historical interpretation, formal analogy
sources.claim: Narrative propagation, decay, recurrence and adoption should be studied separately from simple valence.
sources.causal_strength: Research program, not an identified narrative-return elasticity.
limitations: Historical selection and endogenous narratives
Epidemic model is an analogy with application-specific assumptions
No production diffusion parameters inferred

sources.title: Evidence for Countercyclical Risk Aversion: An Experiment with Financial Professionals
sources.version_read: Published paper hosted by an author
sources.read_depth: Boom/bust randomization and fixed-choice-environment design, risk versus ambiguity tasks, fear manipulation and threat-versus-realized-shock results.
sources.evidence_type: Randomized priming and controlled fear experiments
sources.claim: Bust priming can increase fear and reduce experimental risk taking with the financial choice set held fixed.
sources.causal_strength: Randomized treatment supports within-experiment causal effect; population and market transport require care.
limitations: Primed scenario is not a full crisis
Aggregate equilibrium and real leverage not experimentally identified
Mediation claims require their own assumptions

sources.title: The Neural Basis of Financial Risk Taking
sources.version_read: Published author-hosted paper
sources.read_depth: Dynamic-task design/risk-neutral benchmark, anticipatory-activation regression discussion, results and interpretation around pp. 766–768.
sources.evidence_type: Neural association with subsequent choices in controlled task
sources.claim: Anticipatory neural activity predicts distinct risky/riskless choices within the task.
sources.causal_strength: Temporal prediction and controls, not direct experimental manipulation of brain activity.
limitations: Small laboratory sample
Normative mistake classification depends on risk-neutral benchmark
No inference from market text to individual neural state justified

sources.title: Risk, Ambiguity, and the Savage Axioms
sources.version_read: Published university-hosted copy
sources.read_depth: Urn-choice construction, explicit nonexperimental qualification, and ambiguity/reliability discussion around pp. 658–661.
sources.evidence_type: Decision-theoretic counterexample and informal choice evidence
sources.claim: Reliability of probability information is distinct from the magnitude of known risk.
sources.causal_strength: Foundational conceptual challenge, not modern randomized causal market evidence.
limitations: No direct market return effect
Ambiguity is not synonymous with variance or disagreement

sources.title: Social Identity and Preferences
sources.version_read: Published manuscript indexed text plus NBER version record; full-text NBER endpoint inconsistently returned April 2008 and September 2009 drafts
sources.read_depth: Published indexed abstract/introduction/results excerpts; full-text experimental randomization and elicitation design; older-draft theoretical salience framework. Detailed obsolete demographic findings excluded.
sources.claim: Identity salience may change measured choices in context; published summary does not support a universal gender-risk effect.
sources.causal_strength: Within-experiment randomized effects; externally generalizing identities or population averages is not justified.
limitations: Version discrepancy explicitly quarantined
Direct PMC page returned browser challenge, not bypassed
Published excerpts rather than complete final text inspected
No individual demographic profiling or universal direction inferred

sources.title: Investor Sentiment and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
sources.version_read: Published full-text HTML
sources.read_depth: Section I theoretical channels, data characteristics, six-proxy PCA construction and macro orthogonalization, cross-sectional results, conclusion.
sources.evidence_type: Aggregate-proxy and conditional cross-sectional return evidence
sources.claim: Sentiment-associated effects vary with valuation subjectivity and arbitrage difficulty.
sources.causal_strength: Predictive conditional evidence, not random assignment of sentiment.
limitations: Composite includes price/issuance variables
Selected macro controls do not identify pure sentiment
Historical index definition is not assumed to equal current vendor series

sources.title: The Limits of Arbitrage
sources.version_read: Published university-hosted paper; publisher full-text excerpts also inspected
sources.read_depth: Capital-risk distinction, delegated-capital mechanism, fully invested equilibrium/Propositions 3–4, liquidation condition and conclusion.
sources.claim: Performance-related capital withdrawal may reduce stabilizing activity when mispricing deepens.
sources.causal_strength: Conditional model result, not unconditional empirical frequency.
limitations: Requires specified capital/performance mechanism
Convergence trading is not necessarily riskless arbitrage
Fundamental-value identification remains difficult

sources.title: Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity
sources.version_read: Author-hosted paper; PDF has prepublication pagination and journal metadata verified on author landing page
sources.read_depth: Introduction and Section 3.2 liquidity spirals, Proposition 5, margin/loss amplification conditions and stabilizing versus destabilizing cases.
sources.claim: Funding constraints and market illiquidity can reinforce one another under stated conditions.
sources.causal_strength: Model mechanism, not a causal estimate of current stress sensitivity.
limitations: Margin dynamics are condition-dependent
Observed volatility alone does not identify funding stress
Own financing capacity must be modeled for trade applications

sources.title: What Explains the Stock Market's Reaction to Federal Reserve Policy?
sources.version_read: 2004 FEDS working paper; published record verified
sources.read_depth: Sections 2.1–2.2 futures-surprise construction and event timing, endogeneity/outlier discussion, level-versus-timing surprise results, limits of excess-return interpretation.
sources.evidence_type: Futures-based event study and return decomposition
sources.claim: Expected policy actions and unexpected components must be distinguished; event timing and prior expectations matter.
sources.causal_strength: Surprise design improves identification but requires orthogonality/endogeneity assumptions.
limitations: Historical monetary regime
Outlier sensitivity
Information effects and simultaneous news
Risk-premium versus overreaction interpretation not uniquely resolved
